paper.title_en: Growth of structure in holographic dark energy models: a posterior predictive comparison
paper.abstract_en: Structure formation has been used to test the viability of the IR cutoff in the Tsallis holographic dark energy (THDE) model, and the future event horizon was found to be a viable IR cutoff (Phys. Rev. D 113, 123531 (2026)). Motivated by this, we constrain the HDE, THDE, and BHDE models using the combined Pantheon+ SN Ia, OHD, DESI DR2, and CMB distance prior datasets, and propagate the MCMC posterior samples into the linear growth sector to obtain the predicted $fσ_8(z)$ and $S_8(z)$ histories under the smooth dark energy approximation. We find that the growth predictions of HDE and BHDE are nearly indistinguishable, while those of THDE lie lowest. A posterior predictive $χ^2$ comparison shows that current $fσ_8$ measurements are statistically consistent with all three models, whereas the $S_8$ comparison yields markedly larger $χ^2$ values for HDE and BHDE and a value for THDE close to that of $Λ$CDM. As an illustrative diagnostic, we construct the $(fσ_8, S_8)$ plane and find that the trajectories of THDE and $Λ$CDM reach the vicinity of the current data region, while those of HDE and BHDE do not. Our results indicate that structure growth observables provide a promising probe for discriminating among holographic dark energy models, while a definitive discrimination will require a joint background and growth likelihood and consistent growth measurements.
